junior.reviewer: claude-opus-5-5 (prompt 05, junior reader, fresh read, content_version 1)

issues.quote: The cleanest rollback is resetting the branch to the last good commit and force-pushing.
issues.text: force-push is not in known_vocab, not in Core concepts, and the git prereq summary covers only revert, reset and reflog. The bold misconception uses it before the correction explains it, and q4 and q5 option d depend on it.
issues.fix: Turn the existing sentence 'force-pushing makes the server's branch point where yours does, even if commits on the server are dropped' into a one-sentence Core concepts entry (proposing force-push for this lesson's vocab in track.yaml), or move this lesson after the lesson that introduces force-push.

issues.quote: The server's `main` now holds nothing theirs lacks, so Git accepts their ordinary push without a force, and the bad commit is back on the server.
issues.text: I cannot get from 'holds nothing theirs lacks' to 'Git accepts their ordinary push'. Neither known_vocab nor the git prereq summary says when Git accepts or refuses an ordinary push, so the 'so' has no rule behind it for me. q4 option c rests on this step.
issues.fix: Add one sentence before 'The server's `main` now holds nothing theirs lacks' stating the rule: Git accepts an ordinary push only when your branch already contains every commit the server's branch has; otherwise it refuses.

issues.quote: Teammates' local copies of `main` still hold the bad commit under their new one.
issues.text: Re-read twice: 'their new one' refers to a commit the teammates have not made yet in the story. I only understood it after reading the 'You notice this when…' sentence.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: 'A teammate who pulled before the reset still has the bad commit in their local `main`; their next commit goes on top of it.'

issues.quote: at first the api is `Progressing`, not `Healthy`.
issues.text: 'At first' implies the health changes later, but the lesson never says to what. I am left wondering whether it later becomes something else and whether that matters for the rollback.
issues.fix: Either drop 'at first' or add half a sentence saying what health the Application shows if the Pod keeps failing to pull.

issues.quote: While automated sync is on, Argo CD refuses it. So the way back goes through the repository.
issues.text: The refusal is stated with no reason, so q2 is a rule I memorise rather than understand. I also cannot picture how a person would request this rollback.
issues.fix: After 'Argo CD refuses it', add one clause giving the reason in terms already taught (automated sync, what Git names).

issues.quote: Lines 9–10, above the excerpt, set `good` to the tag the clone names, `1.0.0` here, and `bad` to a tag of zeros.
issues.text: 'the clone' is used here, but what the clone is (the working clone) is explained only in the next sentence. I paused on it.
issues.fix: Say 'the working clone' here and move the parenthetical '(the script's own local copy of the config repository, with its full history)' to this first mention.

issues.quote: Whoever wrote it mistyped the commit hash that CI's `sha-…` tags carry.
issues.text: The situation is a mistyped hash, but the script and output use a hash of all zeros. I briefly wondered whether the zeros are the typo or a stand-in. Section 5 says 'a tag of zeros' without linking it back to the situation.
issues.fix: In section 5, after 'and `bad` to a tag of zeros', add 'standing in for the mistyped hash'.

issues.quote: Line 30 waits for the new Pod to report an image pull error
issues.text: The k8s prereq taught ImagePullBackOff; the output and q3 show ErrImagePull. The code greps both, and the prose does not say how they relate, so I wonder whether ErrImagePull is a different failure.
issues.fix: Extend the sentence with one clause saying that ErrImagePull and ImagePullBackOff are both shown for the same failed image pull.

issues.quote: Commit the tag of the fixed image to `envs/staging` and let automated sync apply it.
issues.text: The correct option nearly repeats the lesson's sentence 'commit the tag of an image that fixes the bug and works with the new schema, and let automated sync deploy it', so it can be picked by matching wording.
issues.fix: Reword option b so it does not mirror the lesson sentence, e.g. 'Point staging at the image CI built for the fix, by a commit to the config repository.'

issues.quote: A teammate who pulled the bad commit could bring the bad tag back with their next push.
issues.text: Option c almost repeats 'You notice this when a teammate who pulled the bad commit pushes their next commit and the bad tag is back.' Because of the push-rule gap in section 6, I can pick it only by matching the sentence, not by reasoning.
issues.fix: Once the push rule is in section 6, reword option c to describe the mechanism (an ordinary push from an older clone is accepted) instead of mirroring the lesson sentence.
